name: East Face Direct
descent_text: Once the route rejoins the standard East Face partway up, descend as for that route: downclimb/rappel with a single rope, carrying spare webbing for old anchors.
approach: Same as the standard East Face: Pete Lake Trailhead (2,800 ft) via Pete Lake Trail/PCT and the Chimney Creek climber's path to high camp at Sunrise Knob (~4,600-4,800 ft).
overview: A harder, more direct 1954 variation of the East Face that climbs solid 5.6 rock through the lower face — avoiding the loose ('choss') sections of the standard route at the cost of a moat crossing — before rejoining the East Face about halfway up.
beta: Solid 5.6 climbing that rejoins the East Face route about halfway up. Instead of the standard route's loose rock, this variation deals with a moat, which parties cross by building a snow anchor with a picket and jumping the gap. Nine pitches in all, mostly fourth class with short easy fifth-class steps.
